Every day, we’re advancing the frontiers of what’s possible with our all-electric lineup. #1 Broadest range of EV models to choose from4 13 Electric vehicle models across our brands 2nd Largest volume of EVs sold in the U.S.5 Find the EV for your drive View important information.6-17 Solutions to power your world At home and on the road, you deserve freedom. GM Energy gives you the smart power you need as you live, work, and explore. Leading the charge in electrification “I’m grateful to be surrounded by our talented team here and world-class battery technology infrastructure that puts us in a great position for industry leadership. Let’s keep driving forward.” Kurt Kelty, VP of Battery, Propulsion, and Sustainability Kelty is a globally recognized leader in battery technology. Since joining GM in 2024, he’s helped push the boundaries of battery innovation and propulsion technology. Destination: electrification Powerful partnerships, manufacturing innovations, and a charging network poised for exponential growth. We’re making sure the future for EVs is bright. Pioneering battery technology The award-winning LMR battery chemistry we’re developing is expected to bring premium range and performance at a more affordable cost to drivers in the near future Public Charging Commitment We’re leading the charge, partnering with Pilot Travel Centers and EVgo to put public chargers where people need them most Factory Zero We are all in on EVs—with our first, fully dedicated 4.51 million square foot EV assembly plant Spring Hill We’ve invested $2.3 billion in the future of EVs with our second battery cell manufacturing plant Zero emissions. All business. The all-electric walk-in van will now be available and can be serviced at participating certified Chevrolet dealers, offering commercial customers added convenience. BrightDrop EV Van Yes, GM is leading the industry forward with a bold commitment to an all-electric future. We’ve made EVs a top strategic priority across every brand in our portfolio, combining innovation, performance, and design to create electric vehicles for every kind of driver as part of our zero emissions vision. GM Energy is a business run by GM. It is dedicated to expanding how we power our lives on and off the road. It offers energy management solutions like home charging, battery storage, and vehicle-to-home technology that work seamlessly with our electric vehicles. It’s all part of GM’s commitment to building a more sustainable, resilient future. While electric vehicles are a core focus, GM also continues to invest in broad range of vehicles that are created using environmentally friendly practices. An EV (electric vehicle) runs on a battery and electric motor, producing zero tailpipe emissions. An ICE (internal combustion engine) vehicle runs on gasoline or diesel and emits greenhouse gases. At GM, we’re investing in EVs to help drive toward a future with Zero Emissions without compromising on performance, design, or choice. If the vehicle was not used as a courtesy transportation vehicle by your dealer, then the vehicle may qualify for the federal new clean vehicle tax credit under Section 30D of the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). IRS-qualified dealers eligible to offer the tax credit and participating dealers may apply the tax credit at the point of sale toward the vehicle price. See dealer for details and to confirm vehicle tax credit qualification. Your personal eligibility to claim this tax credit depends on your individual circumstances, including whether your adjusted gross income for the current or preceding taxable year exceeds the income thresholds contained in Section 30D. Buyers are advised to obtain a copy of the IRS's confirmation that a "time-of-sale" report was submitted successfully by the dealer. You should consult your tax, accounting or legal advisor to confirm your eligibility or if you have questions regarding this tax credit. This information does not constitute tax, accounting or legal advice. Credit availability and amount subject to federal law and regulations and manufacturing constraints. For information about the IRA’s federal tax credit, please visit https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/taxevb.shtml. **Qualifying vehicles that are purchased by businesses and certain tax-exempt organizations may qualify for the federal commercial clean vehicle credit of up to $7,500 under Section 45W of the Internal Revenue Code. Qualifying vehicles must not have been previously allowed a tax credit under Sections 30D or 45W of the Internal Revenue Code. Eligibility to claim this tax credit depends on the particular circumstances of the entity claiming the credit, including the anticipated holding period for the vehicle and, for certain tax-exempt organizations, whether the organization complies with pre-filing registration procedures required by the Internal Revenue Service. Maximum credit amount may be influenced by the purchase price of a qualifying vehicle, the incremental cost of the vehicle over a comparable vehicle powered by an internal combustion engine, and other factors. You should consult your tax, accounting or legal advisor to confirm your eligibility or if you have questions regarding this tax credit, including how to determine incremental cost.
